For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:
General Visibility Rules:
•	Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
•	"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
•	Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:
•	Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
•	Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
•	High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
o	Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
o	Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
o	Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
•	Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
•	Material and Construction:
o	Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
o	Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
o	Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
•	Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
•	Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Weekly (Fri) Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
description:
Wow! What a great location for a standout! On 5/30, around 17 people, including a bagpiper!  What a blast! LOTS of engagement with motorists!

There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all! 

We'll have letterboards prepared for the lower part of the overpass fencing - the photo shows how that will look to folks passing on the Mass Pike. We're interacting with motorists on the Mass Pike, and on Southampton Road. We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 1/2 hours.

### How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass. 

### Parking

We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and it seems that parking would be OK there.

It looks like The Wealth Technology Group has vacated their office at 130 Southampton Rd, but the internet says that other businesses are located there, so please be mindful if you decide to park there.

### Etiquette!

We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too. 

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

- at the first sign of heat illness (dizziness, muscle cramps, headache, nausea) move to a cooler location and slowly drink a cool beverage. Seek medical attention if you do not feel better. (WA State Dept of Health)

title: Avelo Airline Nationwide Protest
description:
**Indivisible Mesa is joining the Coalition to Stop Avelo's nationwide call to action for a full boycott of Avelo Airlines and organizing protests at all 54 airports where they operate.** Our goal? Drive ticket sales to ZERO and make Avelo feel the consequences of profiting from deportations.

On May 31st, Indivisible Mesa was part of the **26 protests across the country** who came together to protest Avelo Airlines on the same day for the first time! To keep the pressure on Avelo, the Coalition is planning to support additional nationwide protests and Indivisible Mesa is again joining the call!!

**Indivisible Mesa will be protesting against Avelo Airlines operating ICE deportations on Saturday, July 26th!** 

By protesting together, everywhere, on the same day, we elevate our anti-Avelo movement from a local news story to a can't miss national news story!

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨

The message to **Avelo** is simple: **"Cancel your contract with ICE."**

The message to **City Hall** is simple: **"Stop funding Avelo with local dollars."**

The message to **travelers** is simple: **"Boycott Avelo, don't give them your money."**

The message to **allies** is simple: **"Join us. Stand for justice. Fight inhumanity."**

And the message to the **world** is powerful: 
*We stand for families. 
We stand for immigration rights. 
We stand for due process. 
We stand for all Americans who are feeling scared and vulnerable. 
We stand against companies that sacrifice people for profit. 
We stand against blood money and we stand against deals-with-the-devil. We stand against Avelo's contract with ICE. 
And we stand together, together, together. 
We will win this fight! 
We will force Avelo to cancel its ICE contract.**

Protest locally, speak nationally.

✨Be safe, be lawful, be loud. Bring signs. Bring friends. Take pics.✨


==**Protest Information**==

🌄 Indivisible Mesa will be at the intersection of East Ray Rd and Power Rd.

🅿️ There is PLENTY of parking in the store surrounding the intersection, including Walmart, Target, etc. 

❄️Bring all the things to keep yourself cool like cooling towels, umbrellas for shade, water, etc. and feel free to bring extra for other protestors if you are able to!

🔥Indivisible Mesa leadership realizes it may be too hot for some to attend the event, but we have to be outside and as visible as possible. IT'S VITAL. **If this means you can only protest for 20 mins, then please come for 20 mins!! Everybody and every minute counts!!**


==**Signs & Graphics**==
Please create signs and graphics that are relevant to Avelo & Mesa Gateway Airport! The messaging we put on our signs can do a lot to cut right through Mesa Gateway's bureaucratic smokescreen. 

   ☑️ Call attention to Avelo Airlines separating families

   ☑️ Complicity of Mesa/Gateway airport

   ☑️ Illegal deportations without due process

   ☑️ Human trafficking

   ☑️ Rather overheat than let human trafficking continue

   ☑️ Print out large pics of ICE kidnapping people in Phoenix

Please share and bring friends to protest against these flights that are illegal, inhumane, & unconstitutional.

title: Honk & Wave: Tell Avelo Airlines to Cancel ICE Agreement

address_lines: near the intersection of Rt. 13 and School Lane

description:
Co-hosted by 302 United and Indivisible Highlands and Beyond.

Avelo Airlines has accepted a $150 million contract to operate deportation flights, aiding and colluding with the federal government in the illegal removal of individuals without their right to a fair hearing or due process. 

We demand that Avelo Airlines cancels their agreement with ICE immediately. Come out and help us keep up the pressure on AVELO and to promote a boycott until they change course.

Keep the message simple;
use large letters;
and make the letters thick and bold.)

We'll rally on both sides of Rt. 13, so stay on whichever side of the highway you park on. Please do NOT cross the busy highway!

After the Honk & Wave, all are welcome to gather at the IHOP across the street for "Protest and Pancakes!" (You don't have to get pancakes; they have avocado toast and veggie sausage, too!) Join us to connect and converse!!

Parking Options:

Go to Lot D, $7.00 per car, then walk to the nearby sidewalk along the DuPont Hwy. (The first section of Lot D is a quick right turn after passing the ChristianaCare-GoHealth Urgent Care, right next to the Wilmington Airport.The second section of Lot D is a right turn immediately after you past this first turn for lot D.  There is a sign for Lot D at this turn.)

You can create an account online ahead of time so you can complete your payment from home in advance.  We recommend taking this step ahead of time, so you can just park and join us. Go to this link to set up your parking account: https://p-123.com/. Click on the ‘create your account now’ button. You will be asked for the zone ID which is 10500. You will add your license plate number, then pay with a credit card. 
You could also use this same link or a QR code once you arrive to pay.  The signs in the parking lot have this info.
At this link below you can see where Lot D (or Remote lot) is located:
https://www.flyilg.com/parking-wilmington-airport-ilg

Parking is also available behind the IHOP across the street: specifically, try the large shopping area lot between IHOP and Planet Fitness. (Again, if you park there, stay on that side of the road to rally along DuPont Hwy in front of the IHOP. Do NOT cross DuPont Hwy.)

title: A Funeral for the Constitution - A Peaceful Protest of the Inaction of Senator Thom Tillis
description:
Join us on August 23, we will gather in downtown Greensboro dressed in black, not in celebration - but in mourning.
This solemn protest, led by concerned citizens across North Carolina, is a funeral march for our Constitution - the foundational document Senator Thom Tillis continues to undermine and nullify, piece by piece.
As we carry a symbolic coffin through the streets, accompanied by the haunting sound of a lone bagpipe, we will grieve the erosion of civil liberties, voting rights, and democratic norms. This is not a spectacle. This is a eulogy - for fairness, for accountability, and for a government of the people.

With peaceful resolve and powerful symbolism, we will honor what has been lost and demand better from those elected to serve us. We mourn, we march, and we resist - because democracy should not die in silence.

title: NO NUKES VIGIL - Every Friday
description: The Santa Fe chapter of Veterans For Peace started this vigil in 2002 and have continued it every Friday at noon for 23 years. Its purpose is to bring awareness to the hundreds of billions of our tax dollars going to the production of new nuclear weapons here in our state. Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Each pit, on average, has the destructive power of 20 Hiroshima-sized bombs. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

title: Standing up for Democracy and Social Justice - Estacada - Every Saturday From 11am to Noon
description:
Every Saturday from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM, we gather for an hour of peaceful visibility on the corner of Highway 224 and City Hall in Downtown Estacada.

We’d like to believe we’re standing in peace — but these days, we’re standing in protest and for our democracy.

It’s fun. It’s energizing. And honestly? It’s better than doing nothing.
This may be our last chance to stand up for our rights — locally, visibly, and together. No one’s coming to save us. It’s up to us to lead. And the best place to start is right here in our own community.

✨ What to expect:
– Supportive honks and waves from passing cars
– Friendly conversation and good company
– Bring a sign if you want — or just bring yourself
– It’s only one hour, but it means something

It might feel small — but it’s something. And sometimes something is everything. Please join us. There’s real power in showing up

title: Weekly (Tues) I-91 Overpass Standout - Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Bring a friend!!!

Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee visited twice in the three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue. We haven't seen him lately, but...

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

description:
This a local Indivisible West CoCo County event!

 "Speak up, speak out, get in the way. Get in good trouble, necessary trouble, and help redeem the soul of America.” That was the message from the legendary John Lewis to all of us who fight for justice and freedom. It is that message that we carry with us as we face the greatest threat to our freedom and democracy since the Civil War. 

Join us every Friday, 5pm – 6pm at the corner of San Pablo Dam Road and Appian Way. We bring the hope and commitment carried by John Lewis throughout his life to the streets of our West County community. 

FOOD, TOWEL & TOILETRIES DRIVE: If you can, bring a can or box of food for our community (no glass) &/or shower amenities for the unhoused in our local community.

Bring signs, peaceful energy, friends, flags, chants, etc.

"Do not get lost in a sea of despair. Be hopeful, be optimistic. Our struggle is not the struggle of a day, a week, a month, or a year, it is the struggle of a lifetime. Never, ever be afraid to make some noise and get in good trouble, necessary trouble," Congressman John Lewis.

title: Rally in Mentor to say NO to Cuts, Raids, and War--Congressman Joyce--HELP!!
description:
Come and join members of Ohio District 14 as we stand together to protest the harmful actions of the Trump Administration.     We gather every Friday from 10-11:30 along Mentor Avenue in Eleanor Garfield Park to say that we do not approve of Donald Trump's plan to cut funding for vital programs like Medicaid and Snap.  We do not approve of Donald Trump's plan to tear families apart by forcibly removing non-dangerous immigrants in our communities.   And we do not approve of Donald Trump (who called himself the "Peace President") bombing Iran without the approval of Congress and the people of the United States.   

We have reached out to Congressman Dave Joyce with our concerns about the harm of the Trump Administration, but we have not heard back with specific and reassuring responses.  And we have questions for the Congressman.  We want to know why Congressman Joyce voted to cut Medicaid and Snap.   We want to know why Congressman Joyce is allowing the Trump administration to terrify immigrants in our communities.  We want to know why Congressman Joyce did not take a stand against bombing Iran--an aggressive move that could be the start of the United States going to war in the Middle East.   All of these actions will cause harm to Congressman Joyce's constituents.  

***Congressman Joyce, we want you to stand up for the health, wellbeing, and safety of your constituents.  Please come and join us.  We need your help saying "NO" to the harmful behavior of the Trump administration. ***

Attendees:
Please bring friends and family and family-friendly signs.  Children have been joining us now that school is out.

Feel free to bring a chair, and join for any amount of time you are able.    Please park in the lower lot and walk up the hill to our protest site if you are able.   Leave the upper lot open for elders and families with young children.  Please do not park on the grass as vendors need to set up in this area for the Mentor Farmers Market.   

If you are able, please bring non-expired food and personal care items to donate to our local food pantries.   Food items include canned proteins, peanut butter and jelly, canned fruits and vegetable, and shelf stable food items such as grains, pasta, and cereal.  Personal care items include hand soap, toilet paper, tissues, paper towels, tampons, and diapers.


*A core principle behind all events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants not to engage with drivers, passers-by, and counter protestors who have different ideas than ours and show this in an unkind manner.  We will not return the hurt and anger.  We have an opportunity to show kindness and bridge the divide.  Let's take this opportunity.  Our nation needs this.*

This event is hosted by Ohio District 14 Partners--A coalition of pro-democracy groups in Ohio District 14.    June 27th marked our 20th event.

***Note--This event used to be held in front of the building that houses Congressman Joyce's office--8500 Station St., The Matchworks Building.   We used to enter the building in small groups to talk with the staff members in the Congressman's office while others protested on the sidewalk in front of the building.  Our group grew from 3 people to 60 people in 8 weeks.    We were not permitted to park in the lot in large numbers, so we decided to move to Eleanor Garfield Park.   

Individuals are permitted to park and enter the Matchworks Building to talk to staff members in the Congressman's Office on the third floor on M-F from 9-5.   We strongly encourage you to do this.  This action is a great way to protect and improve democracy.

title: March for Integrity (Carson City)
description:
The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: March for Integrity (Detroit)
description:
**Co-Hosted by:** [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/), [Indivisible Macomb Defenders Rising](https://macombdefenders.com/), [Indivisible Fighting 9](https://indivisiblefighting9.com/), [We the People Dissent](https://wethepeopledissent.com/), [ShowMItheMoney](https://showmithemoney.org/), [50501 MI](https://linktr.ee/50501Michigan), [Mop Up Michigan](https://mopupmichigan.org/), [Michigan United Action](https://miunitedaction.org/)

The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: Forests for Indy - March from IFA to the City-County Council Meeting on Monday July 7th
description: Summer is here and we are more grateful than ever for our urban forests and the relief they provide us. It is also budget season, and our forests need our help to continue helping us! Unfortunately, Indianapolis continues to lose urban forests and canopy and all the benefits they provide - heat mitigation, carbon capture, storm water management, beautification and quality of life. There is only one way that this destruction ends - with forest friends demanding change. Please join our "Forests for Indy" volunteers and march to the Council meeting to do exactly that. The Councilors see and notice us and our advocacy makes a difference. We are pushing for: the creation of a "forest fund" (Marion County Urban Forest Preservation Fund), for an agency to manage this fund and properly steward the remaining forest in Marion County, and for the allocation of money in the 2026 budget for the acquisition of urban forest.

title: Copy of: Mondays @ McCormick's
description:
This is an EMERGENCY! Senate Protest Event in Philadelphia Continues This Week and For the Foreseeable Future.

Now called "Mondays at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - Here's why:

We are living in a MAGA-republican Coup. We were warned. Now it's here!

Here at home our democratic rights are being eroded and the Trump/Musk team is putting us all in danger. The limits of Executive power against the courts are being tested every day. If Trump decides to ignore the courts, there is very little they can do to enforce their decisions and unless Congress acts, it would be a true constitutional crisis. (And so far, Congress is controlled by the MAGA movement and the Democrats have not done enough to stand up and fight back.) It could even spiral down into outright civil war as competing factions and states careen between untested solutions to protect their own interests and those of their constituents and funders. There is real harm being done across the entire domestic sector. Layoffs, program cuts for the needy and for the average US resident, persecution of law abiding immigrants and students and other activists for simply speaking their mind and organizing constitutionally protected protest. Fear is also their weapon.

Our international role is being flipped on its head - yes, the US has always had a questionable foreign policy, providing aid and promoting democracy and human rights - to a degree - on the one hand, while at the same time invading other countries for the good of corporate profits and geopolitical dominance. Trump considers a policy to outright invade counties like Mexico and Greenland in violation of international law and to extend US power - A clear expression of Empire! Trump is considering power grabs not unlike those that the Nazi regime in Germany perpetrated in search of "Lebensraum", (Living Space) a euphemism for territorial conquest. And they got away with it (for a while) because the people who stood up were either jailed, exiled or murdered. The rest were either regime supporters (Like the solid 30% base of the MAGA movement) or went along out of fear of retribution. We cannot let fear prevent us from standing up this time. History will judge us.

We now have a true oligarchy in the US and we must fight back!

The Trump administration’s illegal actions and relentless efforts to dismantle protections for vulnerable communities — both here in the U.S. and abroad— have made clear we are in the midst of an authoritarian takeover not unlike what has happened in Orban’s Hungary. 

His plan to "Own Gaza" and move out Palestinians is NOT a plan to destroy Hamas and increase Israeli security - it is ETHNIC CLEANSING pure and simple. It's a land grab. All for development rights and to secure a seaport access to natural gas deposits off the shore of Gaza in the Mediterranean Sea. The Levant gas field includes the shores of historic Palestine (Israel and Gaza), Syria, Lebanon and, on the opposite side, the island of Cyprus. This field is estimated to contain about 122 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. So it will accelerate the climate emergency. 

As we all know Trump/Musk plan to get rid of a number of government agencies that protect our health, livelihood and constitutional rights. - the EPA is on the hit list. The Department of Education is too. So, is the CDC, the NIH and many other important agencies that protect the US public.

As we all know - thousands have already been fired, causing chaos and havoc and real harm to both dedicated civil servants AND people served by life affirming programs voted on by the U.S. people and enacted, in most cases, by the U.S. Congress. The Administration may have authority to make staffing decisions, but as is the case with the Department of Education - many of these agencies can only be eliminated by acts of Congress - Trump has overstepped his legal authority.

Thankfully, the courts have, so far, acted as a check on much of Trumps clear and blatant abuses of executive power. But we cannot count on the courts, particularly the US Supreme court, which has been stacked by Trump appointees and ideologues friendly to executive power. 

Resistance is NOT futile - it is essential. 

We are launching "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - we will assemble peaceably - as is our constitutional right - outside Senator McCormick's Philadelphia office until Senator McCormick agrees to meet with us and support our demands: (These will change as conditions develop)

 1 - Stop voting for legislation inspired by Trump's project 2025 agenda - a plan to slash Medicaid, gut school lunch programs, and shut down nursing homes while handing more power to billionaires like Elon Musk. 

2- Roll back Trump's mean spirited and Unconstitutional funding pauses. Shutting down USAID is already killing people in need all over the World. Cuts to programs here in the US could do the same. Funding for these programs are up to the Congress and the US people to decide, not Trump! 

That's just for starters. Overall we want Senator McCormick to represent us all, not just his rich friends. We want Senator McCormick to DO HIS JOB!
The stakes could not be higher. The administration is pushing an authoritarian agenda that threatens our democracy, our rights, and the well-being of millions here at home and around the planet. 

We have the power to resist—and we must use every tool at our disposal to stop them.

title: Good Trouble Rally!
description:
### Join Indivisible Greater Vancouver (IGV) and MoveOn-Clark County for a peaceful rally to show the power of getting in "Good Trouble"!
We gather together peacefully to say no to the authoritarian agenda destroying our country. The People hold the power, and we demand the rule of law,  our civil and human rights, as well as restoration of our safety net and slashed government programs. 

We'll meet at 6916 NE Fourth Plain Blvd in Vancouver, staying on public property. Park on the street or in the surrounding neighborhood. Bring a sign, noisemakers, and your voice to let everyone know we stand united against authoritarians!

### Safety tips for attending rallies in hot weather:

- wear a wide brimmed hat and light colored, breathable clothing

- drink plenty of water

- at the first sign of heat illness (dizziness, muscle cramps, headache, nausea) move to a cooler location and slowly drink a cool beverage. Seek medical attention if you do not feel better. (WA State Dept of Health)

Your safety is our top concern. If you need assistance, visit our first aid tent, reach out to one of our Community Responders in orange vests, or contact the organizers.  If you are concerned about your ability to stand or walk outside during hot temperatures, please stay home!


We at IGV strongly believe that peaceful, non-violent activism offers social movements the most power to effect change. Through peaceful protests, we set an example of making our voices heard with dignity, empowered by truth. IGV does not condone intimidation, threats, vandalism, interference with access to a business, or any other lawless actions. If instigators or our opponents attempt to violate our commitment to non-violence, we will try to de-escalate them and will end the event if needed to maintain a safe environment.

title: Labor Day 2025
description:
Throughout our history, the labor movement has had the vision to imagine a life for working people that didn’t exist yet, and the will to make it happen. When we fought for an eight-hour work day, they called it unrealistic. When we said we demand health and safety measures because our jobs shouldn’t kill us, they said the bosses would never give in. But our collective power made it happen.  

Every organizing campaign, every strike is an act of radical hope. We bet our solidarity and our collective power that working people can live a better life—one where they don’t have to struggle to afford food, housing, and health care, where no one is targeted for who they are or where they were born, where we can raise children and retire in dignity. 

That hope in the dark times, that vision for a better, fairer future—the American people believe in it too. Over 70% of Americans and nearly 9 in 10 young people support unions. 

Workers built this country and we have the power to take it back. An economy, a government, and a country for the people, not the billionaires. In the streets and on the shop floor, in union halls and the halls of Congress, working people are rising up and fighting for freedom, fairness, and security. 

This Labor Day, we’re going to show the billionaires and big corporations who we are and how we fight. We will stand together to speak up. Speak out. Demand better. And we WILL take our country back!

More event details to follow!

Sponsored by Pierce County Central Labor Council, AFL-CIO

title: Resistance: Defend Democracy, No Kings Rally
description:
No Kings! Reclaiming Our Democracy!

Good morning, patriots! We're here again, loud and proud, for our weekly Saturday Rally because we refuse to stand by while the promise of America slips away. "No Kings!" isn't just a slogan; it's a declaration that we are here to stand against authoritarianism and reclaim a government **by the people, for the people.** We will not be silent while fundamental rights are stripped away and power goes unchecked.

Our protest today, and every Saturday, is a resounding **call to action** against:

* **Leaders who believe they are above the law.** No one is above the Constitution.
* **Policies that undermine free and fair elections.** Our vote is our voice, and it must be protected.
* **Attacks on our personal freedoms and civil liberties.** We will not surrender the rights that define us as Americans.
* **Corruption and the prioritizing of special interests over the common good.** Our government should serve all of us, not just a select few.

Let's raise our voices together for **truth, transparency, and equality under the Constitution.** This Fourth of July, and every day, *we* are the true patriots. We are standing together for a future where democracy thrives for everyone!

Ready to join a community that's making an impact? Visit our Linktree! You can easily sign up for our newsletter to hear about upcoming events and initiatives, or consider making a donation to help us cover essential costs like venues and water. Your support helps us create meaningful experiences for everyone.

title: Political Rally for Democracy
description:
**Welcome to the Political Rally for Democracy**

People from all political backgrounds are welcome to join us in a brisk scenic drive in the St. Croix River Valley. The rally is held on open roads, always below the speed limit. We will end with a rockin' house party with chili, beverages, and, if weather permits, a bonfire in Scandia where you can respectfully discuss current events, meet your neighbors, and make friends you didn't know you always needed!

**What's a rally?**

_Yes, it's a pun. It's not a protest; it's a precision driving competition!_ Each car will have two people, a driver and a navigator. At sign-in you will receive a simple paper roadbook that looks a lot like MapQuest/Google Maps directions. Cars leave on minute intervals and will have a chance to check their clock and odometer accuracy at the beginning of the rally. All you have to do is follow the route instructions!

**Following the Course**

Every route instruction will be accompanied by a precise odometer mileage. Most course instructions will be simple and straightforward, like "Right on 1776 St." A couple of turns will be determined by your answers to simple questions about American government. Example: Turn at Stop Sign, Washington Ave. "We the ____" "Billionaires (LEFT)" or "People (RIGHT)"

Start: Not Justa Bar & Cafe, 177 3rd St N, Bayport, MN 55003

End: Scandia, MN

- Sign In: 5 p.m.
- Start Time: 6:01 p.m.
- Total Length: ~50 miles

Suggested donation: $20  ([Online in advance](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/indivisiblescvi936113300) or cash at sign-in)

**Before the rally, you are responsible for ensuring the following are in order:**

- Headlights (high and low beams) and parking lights
- Taillights and brake lights
- Horn, windshield wipers and directional signals
- Rearview mirror
- Foot brakes and parking brake
- Tires (inspect for condition of sidewalls as well as tread depth)
- Seat belts, securely installed for the driver and navigator
- Safety triangle (optional)
- First Aid Kit (optional)
- Tow Rope (optional)
- Fire Extinguisher (optional)

description:
**Co-hosted by:** [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/), [Greater Springfield Indivisible](https://www.greaterspringfieldindivisible.com/)

The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and across the country, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: TeslaTakedown - St. Elmo
description:
**What are we doing?**:

- Protesting Tesla's support for right-wing populist authoritarianism, right here in Austin. 
- Dissuading prospective Tesla customers from buying or leasing new Teslas. 
- Educating onlookers and passerbys about the damage that Elon Musk has done to our democracy and others.

**Why are we doing it?**:

Watch this speech by a ResistAustin organizer that explains the overall reasoning for our Tesla protest campaign: https://youtu.be/uy1JZn_DYcA

**What should you expect?**

- A protest emcee or two
- A medium size group of people consisting of regulars, semiregulars, and newbies
- Supplies with which to exercise your 1A rights, such as markers and posters
- Water and possibly snacks
- A focal point, like the Tesla store, where you may verbally and visually direct your grievances
- Music
- Chanting
- (Uncertain) Counterprotestors
- Here's a video of the "vibe" though we can't promise another piñata! https://youtube.com/shorts/swClQdntgJ0

**What if counterprotestors arrive?**:

"Bullhorn Bully," the serial harasser a.k.a. Will Johnson, most recently visited our protest at Tesla North on 5/24/2025. On that day, he was accompanied by up to 6 members of the WTF biker club, who are documented having aggressively harassed an Austin elected official in 2020, and engaged in an act of attempted intimidation towards ResistAustin earlier this year.

Our guidance is to ignore and/or quietly document Mr. Johnson - he appears to get frustrated and lose focus when no one is engaging with him - he needs protestors to be provoked for his livestream to be entertaining to his audience.

Here are some results of documenting his actions:
https://youtube.com/shorts/CfdwxO-CVoo
https://youtube.com/shorts/nqxoHfibGsY
https://youtube.com/shorts/h_amC8QPm6M

To aid in our effort document counterprotestors like Mr. Johnson, please "extensively document" any suspicious, harassing, or menacing behavior via photo/video and send the recordings with a brief description of your observations to our email inbox, info@resistaustin.us

**What should you bring?**

(Basic)
- Water in a light thermos or water bottle
- Snack
- Sunscreen
- Hat and/or sunglasses
- Light backpack to carry all of the above

(Medium)
- Homemade sign w/ or w/o a handle

(Advanced)
- Bullhorn/megaphone

**Where should you park?**

Tesla St. Elmo is at 500 E. St. Elmo Rd as you turn into a restaurant and brewery center called The Yard. 

You can get to St. Elmo Rd from Congress/275 or the Frontage of I-35-S. You can also get to it from Ben White/71 East Frontage. It is in an industrial park with no street curbs. 

If you are not a customer of a business in the center, you might find limited parking along St. Elmo off the side of the road between Willow Springs and Lucksinger Lane. Otherwise, turn down Lucksinger Lane and head to Sheraton Ave. There is parking at Battle Bend Park or on neighborhood streets on Sheraton Ave or Rowland Drive. It is ½ a mile walk from Tesla and should take 12 to 15 minutes to walk there.

**Final Thoughts**

Unity and discipline are hallmark principles of successful nonviolent resistance movements and our movement will remain inviting and blameless if we maintain these principles in the face of provocation.

**GENERAL PROTEST/RALLY REMINDERS**

This is a peaceful protest. Remember the ABCs of protesting:

A) Always obey traffic signals and directions of the safety team!

B) Beware of detractors*! Do not talk to detractors or unaffiliated interviewers - doing so increases risks for all of us, including all the volunteers and organizers.

Do NOT yell back at them or gesture (thumbs down, middle finger, etc.) Do NOT post photos or videos of them online. Do NOT reveal any personal or contact info to anyone at this or any rally you do not know to be on your side. If someone becomes threatening or violent, move away quickly and alert a safety volunteer, a police officer, and/or call 911. These guidelines keep you, our volunteers, and our organizers safe. Thank you!

description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Hello, people who care about democracy! Thanks for signing up.

My name is Syd and I call myself the reluctant activist, because I'd really rather be home resting, crocheting and managing my health issues but instead I'm forced to fight fascism in America. I'll be the one with the green walker and the loud voice. 😁

With the rapid assaults on our rights and the government cuts designed to hurt the poor and vulnerable, I feel it's important that we protest this insanity so I have a weekly rally most Saturdays. We meet from 12-1 on the sidewalk in front of the Neill Public Library. It's at the intersection of N Grand and Olson NE across from the Cougar Plaza.

This Big Beautiful Killer Bill is the opposite of what our government should do for the people. Republicans are choosing to let people go hungry, lose insurance and frankly, die. Not to balance the budget, they're doing it to reward the wealthiest.

We won't give up our rights to peacefully protest. We need to remind this administration that it's the people who have the power, it's supposed to be Congress that writes laws and declares war, that protest is legal but human trafficking is not.

I know these are scary times and I appreciate your bravery. I have rallied here multiple times and the most negative thing I have experienced is a few harsh words from a moving vehicle (that I usually can't hear). I simply reply with "I love you!" as loudly as I am able. It's fun and it prevents any hate from sticking to us. Mostly we get a lot of honking and waving. I find it invigorating, especially when we are surrounded by a lot of other rally-goers.

If someone does tries to instigate trouble don't confront them and remain peaceful. Come get me. You can also leave if you need to. Record video if you are able, so that authorities will be able to ID the agitator. It's important that our protest remain on the sidewalk and not block the traffic or crosswalks so we don't give the police a reason to arrest anyone.

I'm not downplaying the new steps towards full fascism this administration has taken and I don't want you to. Please take the necessary steps to protect yourself.

Again, I expect no problem at our little event, I expect colorful, creative signs, some chanting and numbers of like-minded people who care about our country. If you have any streamers or pinwheels to attach to your signs, please do.There's almost always a breeze. Get your feelings out on your signs, enjoy the marker fumes and chalk dust. Bring water. I bring a partially frozen water bottle on the hot days 

If you have any questions contact me here

p.s. Despite what Tr*mp and Fox News say, I have never received a paycheck for rallying against his theft of power, but I have noted his history of projection. Has he paid people to rally for him?

description:

Rage Against the Regime is a national day of nonviolent action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people.

The 3.5% Rule: A Tiny Percent. A Massive Impact. You are the power.

In the U.S., that’s about 12 million people. It sounds like a small slice of the population—but it’s still millions of us. Millions who are willing to stand up, speak out, and move together.

That kind of change doesn’t come from one big moment. It comes from ordinary people showing up—again and again—with courage, with hope, and with each other.

That’s why our rallies matter. That’s why your presence matters. We’re not just inviting people—we’re counting on them. Because every person adds weight. Every sign, every chant, every step taken together—it all adds up to power.

You’re not alone. You’re not too small. You’re part of the tipping point.
We are. Together.

Stand with us at the entrance to the regional headquarters of the VA Central Western Massachusetts Healthcare System to support our veterans and all federal workers!  We'll be in a high traffic area at a busy light that offers great visibility with veterans and employees turning into the VA entrance.  This is a great opportunity to tell federal workers we support them, while protesting DOGE and Project 2025 cuts that will, if the Trump administration succeeds, eventually erode the VA system and turn it into a privatized system, hurting all veterans who rely on VA for their health care. The administration will slash more than 80,000 jobs under a major restructuring plan that the agency intends to carry out by August to meet a Trump executive order for downsizing the federal government. About a third of all federal workers are veterans.    

Come out to show that ordinary people can raise our voices against the chaos and destruction of this administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there are lots of people, including veterans and their family members, who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and  the GOP.

title: 50 Days of Shame Protest Rally - Rep. Jen Kiggans

address_lines: Main Street and Town Center Drive

description:

The address listed here is inaccurate. Meet at the corner of Main Street and Town Center Drive, Virginia Beach, VA. title: Out of CECOT — El Salvador Consulate Protest

location.venue: Corner of Birch & Millenia (navigate to Panera in Otay Lakes)

description:
THIS IS AN UPDATED DESCRIPTION - We are shifting gears a bit!  

See below's Press Release:

Thursday July 24, 2025 10 to 11:30 


July 24 is El Salvadoran President Bukele‘s birthday. Let’s make it the most memorable ever for him with a nationwide protest to remind him that there are thousands of us on the ground paying attention and fighting for the rights of human beings!


We will be protesting on the corner of Birch & Millenia in front of the Jack in the Box.  

“ DUE PROCESS FOR YOU. DUE PROCESS FOR ME. THIS IS THE LAND OF LIBERTY.” this will be our rallying cry.

You know what to do. Bring your signs. Bring your voice. Bring your courage. Bring your willingness to create Good Trouble.  

MEDIA ADVISORY
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

San Diego Community Joins Nationwide Protest Against ICE Arrest Practices

WHAT: Protest against recent increase in Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrests

WHEN: Thursday, July 24, 10-11:30 a.m.

WHERE: Corner of Birch Road and Millenia Avenue, Chula Vista (near 1610 Millenia Ave., Chula Vista, CA 91915)

WHO: Indivisible Chula Vista and community membersIndivisible Chula Vista will join an 'Out of CECOT' nationwide day of action Thursday, July 24th to protest what organizers call a dramatic increase in ICE arrests of individuals without criminal convictions.

According to San Diego Union-Tribune reporting, 72% of those arrested by ICE in San Diego in June HAD NO CRIMINAL CONVICTIONS OR CHARGES!!!!

"The Trump administration keeps saying that they are targeting 'the worst of the worst,' that they were only targeting violent criminals, terrorists and gang members," said Janine Manchel, event organizer. 

"Instead, they are arresting children, parents going to work, people attending their immigration hearings. They are tearing families apart, hurting farms and businesses and instilling fear in our communities, all just to meet an arbitrary daily arrest quota of 3,000 per day."

Organizers are calling for:

An end to ICE arrests of individuals without criminal convictionsAn end to immigration enforcement operations that organizers say instill fear and disrupt workplacesAn end to ICE arrests of people attending scheduled immigration hearings

To coordinate any interviews with organizers or community members, please reach out to the media contact below.

MEDIA CONTACT: 

Janine Manchel, Indivisible Chula Vista

title: Day of International Friendship -- Peace Arch, BC/WA -- Peace, Love, and a Handshake
description:
Come join us at Peace Arch Park on August 16th as PLH comes together with organizations across the US-Canada and US-Mexico borders, along with sites across the US, for a series of rallies called Friends Across Borders occurring on the same day, celebrating friendship and solidarity between the US, Canada, and Mexico. We want to show this administration that they may break our formal ties, but we will continue to cherish our personal relationships across borders. 
We will all be meeting at the Peace Arch!

Both Canadians and Americans can attend this event without needing to cross the border. Just make sure to follow the directions below to the corresponding parking lot for your country.

We have friends everywhere.

Flags and messages of FRIENDSHIP and SOLIDARITY are welcome. Meet at the monument!

We encourage all attendees who can to help contribute to the local economies of the border towns while visiting the rally.

Friends Across Borders Movement: https://www.friendsxborders.org/

Discover passes are required to park, although a day pass can be purchased for $10. We will meet at the monument. More info on the park here: https://parks.wa.gov/find-parks/state-parks/peace-arch-historical-state-park

-DIRECTIONS-

From the US:

Take exit 276 off I5 towards Blaine City Center. Once you’ve taken the exit, you’ll come to a roundabout. Take the second exit onto 2nd St. There’s a small street sign that says Peace Arch Park. Be sure not to take the third exit, as this will take you back onto the highway and right up to the border.

The entrance to the parking area is at the end of 2nd St. If you don’t have a Discovery Pass, there is $10 parking fee.

From Canada:

Take exit 1 off Highway 99 towards Beach Rd. Head west along Beach Rd. The Duty Free parking lot will be to your left. Continue past the parking lot. There’s a road that runs behind the Duty Free parking lot called Peace Arch Place. Turn left onto this road (you won’t be able to go any further on Beach Rd anyway as it’s closed). and continue until you get to the Peace Arch Park parking lot. Head to the south end of the parking lot. Walk south to the Peace Arch.

title: March for Integrity (Toledo)
description:
Join The Mockingjay Movement for our march for Integrity with M.O.P
 
The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: OUT OF CECOT - EL Salvador Consulate Protest
description:
What does the President of El Salvador - Bukele - want on July 24, a lavish birthday for the coolest dictator. What do we want? To remind him that there are hundreds of men that were unlawfully rendered to torture prison in his country and WE WANT THEM OUT! Either let them go or send them back to the US.  
Join activists in Denver, Oakland, New York, Arkansas, Chicago, Los Angeles, San Bernardino, and other cities to send a LOUD and CLEAR message to Bukele!
We will all be protesting in front of El Salvadoran Consulates on the same day all around the US to make Bukele’s Birthday a day to remember the suffering of others. Bring your signs and banners to the Consulate in downtown Seattle to let the president of El Salvador know we want these people out.  This will be a sidewalk protest in front of the Consulate. A small group will personally deliver hand written messages asking for the return of the unlawfully detained.

DUE PROCESS FOR YOU. DUE PROCESS FOR ME. THIS IS THE LAND OF LIBERTY! - will be our rallying cry.
You know what to do. Bring Your Signs. Bring Your Voice. Bring Your Courage. Bring Your willingness to create Good Trouble. Here’s the demands and ideas for themes for protest signs:

1.) Release all detainees from the U.S. that the Trump adminstration sent there. (Bring Them All Back!)

2.) Provide all detainees adequate access to their families and legal representation.

3.) Cease to accept detainees from the U.S.
We respect the people of El Salvador and the work of the Consulate to serve their own people. This is not a protest of the Consulate but it is a message to Bukele. We will respect the workers and clients that come to the Consulate for services. We intend that the staff will pass our concerns and passion on to Bukele to let him know there are many in the US public unhappy with his collaboration with Trump. 

Coordinated locally by Wallingford Indivisible and the Seattle Immigrant Rights Project. Other Indivisible and Immigrant Activist groups located in cities with El Salvadoran Consulates are also planning actions at their consulates on July 24, or that week.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

title: NO BILLIONAIRES BAILOUT BILL!
description:
Community Action Fair and Rally! 

💥The billionaires are waging an outright war on all of us! They're not even trying to hide it anymore. It's time to get organized and confront this upside-down system that is rigged for the rich! 

💸💣 Seattle Against War condemns the passage of Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill”, aka the Billionaire Bailout Bill, which will massively cut necessary social services for Americans and transfer it to wars and defense spending. We say – money for jobs and education, not for war and deportation! 

The Trump administration is actively carrying out an onslaught of attacks against our communities. With this bill, an additional $125 billion to the US "defense" spending will further entrench us in senseless war and put money into the pockets of war profiteers. And the massive influx of our tax dollars (to the tune of $30 billion!) to ICE enforcement will lead to a leap in violent repression against immigrant communities, and the gutting of Medicaid and SNAP will make our lives even more difficult in the years to come. Washington State will lose $2 billion in federal Medicaid funding, which equates to roughly 200,000 Washington residents losing medical coverage.  

But more and more people are getting organized and fighting back on multiple connected fronts, whether it is challenging militarism, feeding the people, winning divestment campaigns on pro-war institutions, kicking ICE out of everywhere, or organizing their workplaces. The mainstream news refuse to show the full scale of protests and people fighting ICE raids because it shows that we can fight back and win.

✊Come and join us for a Community Action Fair where you can meet the many organizations with fighting campaigns! Don't leave this event without getting plugged in. It's time to build the broadest possible movement against the billionaires!!

📅 Date: Saturday July 26
⏰ Time: 2:30PM – 5:30PM 
📍Location: Seattle Central College (1701 Broadway, Seattle, WA 98122)

title: DEPORT ICE PROTEST!
description:
We all have been watching as the Trump administration and his allies mock the law and humanity by sending ICE after people in our country in inhumane ways. They are being kidnapped off the streets, not allowed due process which is a CONSTITUTIONAL right, and being sent to what is akin to a concentration camp. ICE is being violent for the sake of being violent while accomplishing these horrific tasks that they have decided amongst themselves will "make America great".

Whether a person is undocumented OR is here legally via a visa, a temporary status, or is a citizen, NONE OF THIS IS OKAY. None of this is humane. This is NOT how we treat people and this is not okay with the people of the United States.

Some stats for you:
- Fewer than 30% of detainees have been convicted of a crime of any type.

- Only about 7% of ICE detainees have violent criminal convictions — lower than the overall U.S. felony rate (~8%), underscoring a mismatch with ICE's boasted focus on violent offenders.

- ICE detains over 59,000 people in U.S. facilities — roughly 140% of funded capacity as of June 23, 2025

- Overcrowding in detention centers has led to severe issues, including:
Use of tents or floors due to lack of beds
Restricted medical care
Limited sanitation
Cellblock overcrowding and delayed recreation
Pregnant detainees denied necessary prenatal care
Care provided to women is often provided without their
informed medical consent

ENOUGH IS ENOUGH!

What can we do????

Several groups in the Fox Valley area (listed below) have come together to hold a protest related to the inhumane treatment that immigrants (and sometimes citizens) are receiving. We plan to have protests at the highway overpasses in Green Bay, Appleton, Neenah, Oshkosh, and Fond du Lac.
We are calling for the end of this inhumane treatment. We are calling for local law enforcement agencies to end their 287(g) agreements with ICE. We are calling for all people, no matter their race or ethnicity, to be treated the SAME under the law.

JOIN US!!

Two unnamed locations in Green Bay. Volunteer via sign up only by emailing info@indivisiblebrowncounty.org to reserve your spot.

title: Community Strike by Immigrants

address_lines: PARK AT FLATIRON PARK ONLY PLEASE

description:
UPDATE: PLEASE PARK CAR AT FLAT IRON PARK FROM NOW ON. THEN WALK TO THE CORNERS. WE ARE NO LONGER ALLOWED TO PARK IN THE PLAZA ON THE CORNER. THANK YOU. 
Los Angeles announced August 12th they will protest for 24 hours against the raids on immigrants in their State of California. This is what an organizer had to say: 
Salas said the community is demanding an end to raids by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement that have been escalating in the Los Angeles area over the past month. She called the raids “a military operation — it is immoral, unlawful and it is purposely cruel.”

“Most importantly, what we are asking is a return of all of those people, all our loved ones, back home,” she said. “We want them back in L.A. We want them in their homes. That’s where they belong, and that’s what our fight is about. … And until those demands come, we will not stop organizing, we will not stop marching. And we call on Congress for accountability and oversight. We will file lawsuits and we will bring common sense to this deranged administration.”

We also have the same raids going on in our State of Arizona and we will stand with California and with all immigrants near and far!

"We have the power of our community and we are going to stop you with the power of the people" 
Written by Salas

title: Families First in Joplin: A Protest and School Supply Drive
description:
📢 OUR MESSAGE:

We are done being sacrificed for billionaires.
 
Indivisible Joplin is partnering with 50501 Missouri to say that our families come first—not billionaires, not authoritarians, and not corrupt politicians. Americans demand an end to policies that harm children, seniors, and our families. We reject the Administration's actions that have gutted essential programs like Medicaid, FEMA, food stamps, school lunches, and more, all so a handful of billionaires can receive tax giveaways. We also stand in solidarity with, and in defense of, immigrant families and those being detained, deported, or disappeared under inhumane policies.
 
We are coming together to say in unity: our families come first.
 
Every Family Matters. Every voice counts.
 
Help us stand to defend the rights and dignity of all.
 
 
🖍 SUPPORTING OUR COMMUNITY:
In the face of a cruel budget that strips resources from families and schools, we are stepping up to support our community and give every child a fair start this school year. Indivisible Joplin will be collecting school supplies for the upcoming school year (K-12) to donate to local school districts. Drop-offs can be made in the parking lot at the rally. Thank you for your generous participation!
 
☮️ COMMITMENT TO NONVIOLENCE:
A core principle behind all Families First events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

If you see any safety concerns, please locate a volunteer in a yellow vest. In the case of an emergency, dial 9-1-1.
accessibility_notes:
Burlison's office is Suite 2.

*It may be a good idea to have the following:

*Protest Sign: Lightweight, sturdy, and easy to carry.

*ID & Cash: Driver’s license or state ID + small bills (phones or cards can fail).

*Water & Snacks: Reusable bottle and energy bars—stay hydrated and fueled.

*Phone & Charger: Fully charged phone + portable power bank.

*First-Aid Kit: Band-aids, pain relievers, any personal meds.

*Mask & Hand Sanitizer: Protection in crowds and clean hands.

*Comfortable Shoes & Clothes: Dress for the weather and wear sturdy footwear.

*Sunscreen & Hat: Sun protection for long days outdoors.

*Videophone: To record key info or contacts. Be sure to turn your Face ID and/or Thumbprint off. Use a 4-6 digit code to lock/unlock your phone.

*Emergency Contacts: Written list in case your phone dies.
*Write an emergency contact phone number in marker on your arm just in case.

title: Families First in Pueblo!
description:
# 🎉 Families First – Pueblo: Community is Power

### ✨ *Power With People Fair + Colors of Justice Vigil*
📍 Pueblo Community College – 900 W. Orman Ave., Pueblo, CO 81004

🗓 Saturday, July 26 | 🕕 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM

## Event Overview
Pueblo is coming together for the **boldest celebration of people power** this summer — and you’re invited!

Join us for **Families First – Community is Power,** part of a nationwide day of action happening in all 50 states. This joyful evening will feature food, games, creative activities, community action, and a glowing tribute to what we’re fighting to protect.

We’ll kick off with the **Power With People Fair** — an interactive space full of:

- 🎯 Fun games for all ages

- 🎨 Art-making, poster creation, and chalk expression

- 📚 Community booths and education stations

- ✍ Hands-on opportunities to learn, take action, and connect

- 🍔 Food and drinks available

- 🧸 Kid-friendly zones for safe, meaningful engagement

Whether you’re brand new to activism or a longtime community builder — this is your space to show up, be seen, and join the movement for justice and care.
## 🕯 Then, as the sun sets…
We’ll gather together for the **Colors of Justice Vigil** — a powerful, peaceful display of unity and light.

Congress may pass devastating cuts to healthcare, food programs, and family support behind closed doors and in the dark — but here in Pueblo, we **shine back in resistance.**

Each participant will receive a **Glow Stick Kit** (suggested $5 donation for ages 18+) as we prepare to light up the night with **colorful solidarity** and community care.

This vigil is our promise:

*We won’t let them take from us in silence. We glow for justice. We rise together.*

## 🧡 Who Should Come?
Everyone who believes in care, dignity, and community.

This is a joyful, welcoming space for:

- Families of all shapes and sizes

- Parents, kids, grandparents, and caregivers

- LGBTQ+ and chosen families

- Immigrant families, neighbors, and advocates

- Students, artists, educators, organizers — and you

## ✨ Why It Matters
The so called “Big Beautiful Bill” cuts what families need most:

- Medicaid and healthcare

- SNAP and school meals

- Housing and disaster relief

- Community safety and support

And it gives even more to billionaires, ICE, and corporate interests.

We’re rising up in Pueblo — with joy, with light, and with the power of community — to say:

**Our families come first. Our communities matter. And we’re not backing down.**

📣 **RSVP now** to be part of this one-of-a-kind experience.

✨ Come for the games. Come for the food. Stay for the fight — and help us shine for justice.

title: Families First Rally!
description:
### Join Indivisible Greater Vancouver and MoveOn-Clark County for a rally to say Our Families Come First!

On July 26, 2025  Indivisible Greater Vancouver and MoveOn Clark County will join with Americans in every corner of the country to come together to demonstrate peacefully  to say: our families come first—not billionaires, not authoritarians, and not corrupt politicians! Collectively we demand an end to policies that harm children, seniors, and our families. We reject the Administration's actions that have gutted essential programs like Medicaid, FEMA, food stamps, school lunches, and more, all so a handful of billionaires can get tax giveaways. We are coming together to say in unity: our families come first.

We'll meet at 6916 NE Fourth Plain Blvd in Vancouver, staying on public property. Park on the street or in the surrounding neighborhood. Bring a sign, noisemakers, and your voice to let everyone know we stand united against authoritarians!

### Safety tips for attending rallies in hot weather:

- wear a wide brimmed hat and light colored, breathable clothing

- drink plenty of water

- at the first sign of heat illness (dizziness, muscle cramps, headache, nausea) move to a cooler location and slowly drink a cool beverage. Seek medical attention if you do not feel better. (WA State Dept of Health)

Your safety is our top concern. If you need assistance, visit our first aid tent, reach out to one of our Community Responders in orange vests, or contact the organizers. If you are concerned about your ability to stand or walk outside during hot temperatures, please stay home!

We at IGV strongly believe that peaceful, non-violent activism offers social movements the most power to effect change. Through peaceful protests, we set an example of making our voices heard with dignity, empowered by truth. IGV does not condone intimidation, threats, vandalism, interference with access to a business, or any other lawless actions. If instigators or our opponents attempt to violate our commitment to non-violence, we will try to de-escalate them and will end the event if needed to maintain a safe environment.

** Stand up for Medicaid with East Portland Saturday morning, July 26th. It's a street protest! This is a National Day of action  ** -American families in every corner of the country will be coming together peacefully to say: our families come first, and we will protect each other.

** Here in Oregon, 1 in 3 of us get our health care through Medicaid, and for kids, it's more than half! **  Everyone, but especially older adults and disabled people – will suffer the consequences of this disastrous decision. title: Reproductive Freedom Friday

address_lines: South Pines Road & East Sprague Avenue

description:
Let's Rally for Reproductive Freedom!

From Pro Choice Washington: "About three years ago, the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) issued its decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization, overturning nearly fifty years of constitutional protections for abortion access under Roe v. Wade.  

In doing so, the SCOTUS decision stripped millions of people of their reproductive freedom. And it opened the door to a sweeping wave of anti-abortion legislation, disinformation, criminalization, and political violence that’s currently playing out across our country. 

In the Dobbs decision, Justice Alito outlined his roadmap to dismantling our right to bodily autonomy and equal rights. Dobbs was just the beginning, as our community saw the continuation of erosion play out last week with the Skrmetti decision. https://prochoicewashington.org/2025/06/20/pro-choice-washington-skrmetti-case/

You have probably also seen the cuts to women's health to include cuts to Planned Parenthood.  I almost feel like this issue has been forgotten.  So... let's remind people!

One of our goals is to give love and support to people and organizations doing the right thing and being courageous.  We have few asks:

1.  Send a thank you card (or postcard) to one or all of the organizations below.  

We have been told by the providers that they SO VERY MUCH appreciate a thank you.  A little bit of gratitude goes a long way.  

Also, we are aware (as of 12/19/2024) that employees at the local Planned Parenthood are considering unionization over what they characterize as low pay and bad working conditions. Here is the full article from Range Media. https://rangemedia.co/planned-parenthood-washington-union/

We believe we can be supportive of patients and providers while also supporting everyone's right to fair pay, good working conditions and the right to unionize.  

Pro-Choice Washington
1916 Pike Place, Ste 12 #1449
Seattle WA 98101

Also, our own Sarah Dixit works for Pro-Choice Washington and is running for Spokane City Council. Here's her website https://www.sarahforspokane.com/ Please support her. We need more people like her in office who are committed to reproductive freedom.

Planned Parenthood Providers and Staff

Peaceful sidewalk rally. Bring signs.   American flags are always wonderful too. Please park carefully with consideration of businesses, etc.

Meet up afterwards 45 Degrees Brewhouse
10421 E Sprague Ave, Spokane Valley WA 99206

Zoe and Amanda

title: Out of CECOT—National Action to Bring our People Home
description:
Out of CECOT is a national day of peaceful action to demand the release of the 250+ men illegally deported to the CECOT. July 24th is President Bukele's birthday, and we’re showing up in San Francisco and at least 10 other cities to demand justice for the hundreds of men he helped the U.S. wrongfully imprison in his country.

Background: On March 15, 2025, the Trump administration secretly transported more than 200 of our Venezuelan community members to El Salvador's maximum-security CECOT prison, a "terrorist confinement center" notorious for human rights abuses. Many came to the United States legally through visas, refugee programs, or seeking asylum, but were ripped from their communities without warning and shipped to a country where they'd never set foot. Their families only discovered their fate when they spotted loved ones in news media photos. Over 3 months later, they remain imprisoned without charges, evidence, or trials, cut off from lawyers and the outside world. President Nayib Bukele actively collaborates in this human rights crisis.

We can't wait. These families need our help now.

WHEN & WHERE: • 4-5pm: Sidewalk protest at the Consulate and deliver handwritten messages for Bukele

• 4:45pm: Walk to City Hall

• 5-6pm: City Hall demonstration with photos and profiles of the disappeared, distributing fliers

We're sending a clear message: The United States Constitution provides due process for every person. We demand that the Salvadoran government:

• Release all detainees from the U.S. that the Trump administration sent to El Salvador.

• Provide a list of all detainees and their health status

• Provide all detainees access to communicate with their families and legal representation

• Cease to accept any more detainees from the U.S.

Important Note: This is not a protest of the Consulates, but it is a message to Bukele. We will respect the workers and clients that come to the Consulate for services. We just want the staff to know that there are many in the US public unhappy with Bukele’s collaboration with Trump.

Please bring signs, banners, and your voice. Help us make Bukele's birthday a reminder that hundreds of innocent men suffer in brutal conditions while their families desperately search for answers.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

More about RANGE Media

RANGE is a media organization for people who love the Inland Northwest and want to make it better. We believe our communities are stronger when our newsrooms are run by truth’s fiercest advocates: the journalists themselves. Since 2020, RANGE has built a newsroom that empowers working people with civic education and people-centered investigative reporting. We are emphatically anti-racist, class-focused and passionate about bridging divides to build solidarity among all people, but especially working people. title: "No Kings" Save Our Democracy
description:
"No Kings"

hosted by 50501 Laguna Beach

Welcome to another "NO KINGS" rally in Laguna Beach.
This event is hosted by 50501 Laguna Beach. 
We will be popping into downtown Laguna for this call to 
activism on Aug 2 at 11:00 am to 3:00 pm.

Please come and go as your schedule allows, join us for a Saturday lunch break on PCH! Please again, no sticks or poles on your protest gear. Laguna PD has a thing for this and it gives them a reason to engage and possibly issue a fine. We have had 6 events without incident and we are proud of our peaceful assembly record.

Sun clothing advised, the beach gets hot and is hard to predict.

Parking is first come, meter, but there are many options that are free like the Trolly and the RIDE / The Local taxi program. Free parking is on Laguna Canyon Rd for commuters, then the Trolly can take you to Main Beach.

Early Birds have more fun, I am usually am there by 10:30.
accessibility_notes:
Main Beach Park in Laguna Beach is very accessible and there are many ways to get there.  

Please park for free in the Canyon and take the trolly.  There is metered parking near the event location but it is first come of course.  Laguna Beach has "The Local" free taxi service.  Uber or Lyft is also advised.  Tow trucks are looking for demonstrations now and get called in by MAGA.  So please don't risk anything.  Bus and Public Transportation is available.  

Public restrooms are available on Forest Ave, Broadway and portables on the beach at Forest Ave.  

Art supplies are available in some supply.  

Water and shade is provided at this location.  Please dress for sun exposure.  The beach is hard to predict but willl start foggy. and burn off, usually around 76 degrees.  

Thank you!

title: Day of International Friendship DETROIT Hart Plaza
description:
The wave of arrests, kidnaps, social cuts, threats, environmental backward steps that we, as the American People, are witnessing and suffering from since January is deeply rooted in hatred. It is painful to watch. It is painful to live with. It is painful to think about the future where we know there is so much work to be done to repair the harm that is currently done to so many individuals and our country. We, because we are proud Americans  believing in the respect of the founding principles of our nation and because we are simply decent humans, will never let hate overtake love.

 We take a stand once again to hammer our values: we love our neighbors, from Canada and Mexico, we love those who come to our country to pick up vegetables in our farms, serve us food in restaurants, study in our universities, and care for our relatives in hospitals, we love the person living next door regardless of their skin color, gender, sexual orientation, because this is what we are fundamentally built to do. Helping and being helped, loving and being loved are the two pillars of human life. Take these out, not one of us would still be here. So, enough with hate. Come join We the People Dissent at Hart Plaza on August 16th for an international day of friendship! Dozens of locations are rallying at the same time across the US. You can check this website out to spot them all! And if you'd like to host one somewhere else in Michigan or in the country, you can do so! https://www.friendsxborders.org.

If you believe in friendship across nations, you will like the pledge we crafted: https://www.friendsxborders.org/sign Don't hesitate to read and sign it!

We will rally at 5 pm when the sun is down a bit to avoid the heat. But please remember to carry a water bottle. Use sunscreen. Last time, we saw lots of you bring an umbrella to create a bit of shade. Great idea! Bring on your umbrellas and signs of love!

There are no restrooms available at the Plaza itself. However buildings around can accommodate us. 

Laz parking garage is available on Bates street along the plaza and there are also two other parking garages off Griswold street that are conveniently located. 

We invite people of good will to join us for a peaceful, positive, and creative demonstration of friendship across borders.  We will affirm the values of peace, friendship, decency, and respect with our North American neighbors!!

title: Salmonberry Trail Guided Hike: Reehers
description:
Wander under a canopy of towering trees in the Tillamook State Forest, where old logging history meets lush rainforest. Keep an eye out for ferns, wildflowers, and the soothing sounds of nearby creeks.

**Getting to Reehers**
- Drive Highway 26 west (or east, depending on where you start) toward Timber Road (just past milepost 38).
- Turn left (south) onto Timber Road, follow for 3 miles into the rural community of Timber.
- Turn right (west) onto Cochran Road in Timber.
- Reehers Camp is 2.2 miles down Cochran Road, a well-maintained gravel road. Drive slowly and respectfully through Timber. 
- Park at the Reehers Camp Day Use Area -- on the left past the campground. Restrooms are available at the parking area, and there is no fee to park, but it is day-use only—no overnight parking or camping allowed.
