title: Disappeared in America Visibility Event:  Yolo County - Three Cities

address_lines: 23 Russell Blvd, Davis OR 1000 Main St. Woodland OR 1110 W Capitol Ave West Sacramento

description:
In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison. Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga.

🚨On Tuesday, August 5, from 4:30-5:30, we’re showing up in Yolo County to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.🚨We will gather at three locations:  In Davis in front of City Hall at 23 Russell Blvd; in Woodland in front of the new courthouse at 1000 Main St. and in West Sacramento in front of City Hall at 1110 W. Capitol Ave. 

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.

Nationwide, a key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions. Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

accessibility_notes:
Transportation

The March begins at Washington Square Park and ends at Union Square Park. Please note that the West 4 Station elevators are closed for renovation and expansion. For subway access, the R/N/W are accessible at Union Square. The M5 bus comes down to Washington Square Park.

 The address for Access-A-Ride at Washington Square Park is 12 Washington Square N.

We offer a variety of accommodations to help make the ADA35 NYC Rally and March accessible to everyone. To request accessibility accommodations, including specific wheelchair and sighted guide requests, please fill out our Accessibility Request Form. You can also sign up to be a marshal through this form.  https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1PE03-N18hxNq4Wp3A6EMhIzwR0Bj1iPBdKzWVxCi2-c/viewform?edit_requested=true

 The deadline to fill out this form and request accessibility accommodations is Friday, July 18.​

​The rally and march will also be livestreamed. More information on the livestream will be available soon!

​ASL Interpretation
An experienced ASL interpreter will translate the rally portion of the event and will be available at the end of the march to help marchgoers communicate with others. 

 COVID-19
While we recognize that some people with disabilities are unable to wear masks, we encourage (but don’t require) participants to wear masks at the event. N95 masks will be available for participants at the start, and marshals will have them to distribute along the route. 

​Sighted Guides
We are happy to offer sighted guides for the march for anyone who needs them. Please fill out our Accessibility Request Form so we can ensure a guide is available for you.

 Wheelchairs
Free wheelchairs are available for all or part of the march for anyone who needs one. Wheelchairs can be pushed by an assigned guide, or if you would prefer a friend or family member, we can simply loan you the chair. Please reserve your chair prior to the march via the accessibility request form, as availability may be limited the day of.

 If there are extra chairs, we are happy to provide them to anyone who needs one, even if they did not reserve one beforehand.

title: Fight Fascism
description:
Romeo Rallies at the Bridge is participating in the nationwide protest against fascism.

This a local Indivisible event!

"Dare to fight fascism" is a call to action, urging individuals to resist the ideologies and practices associated with fascism. 

Why are we here? -

As participants in this protest/demonstration, we commit to the principles of non-violence in thought, word, and action. Our actions are grounded in the belief that peaceful protest is a powerful tool for change.

We will not initiate or participate in any form of violence, including physical assault, property destruction, or verbal abuse. This includes throwing objects, damaging buildings, or any conduct that may incite aggression.

title: Freedom Fridays: RAISE YOUR VOICE ABOVE THE NOISE!
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

Join us on Friday, July 25th at NOON to raise a sign that expresses your voice showing the progressive issue that means the most to you - Women's Rights, Democracy, Ukraine, Voting Right's, Healthcare, Medicare, Climate Change, etc. are a few examples. 

IT WILL BE HOT HOT HOT SO PLEASE DON'T FORGET TO BRING A COLD BEVERAGE. DRESS APPROPRIATELY FOR THE WEATHER, AND BRING A CHAIR IF NEEDED.

COMMUNITY NORMS:
Please read before attending one of our events.

One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. Please remain out of the median, per instructions from the police. Being in the median puts us at risk and potentially drivers as well.

We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day”.

At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept.
Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!

As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers. At larger events, these organizers will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts with yellow safety vests. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

title: Families Over Billionaires
description:
Join us early on Labor Day to honor all the workers of this country— including those working hard without benefit of citizenship— and support labor unions all across the USA! The billionaires of today—with encouragement and support of the current administration in DC— want to exploit workers, bust up unions and energetically, sometimes illegally or violently, discourage new unions from forming. Labor Unions brought us the 40-hour work week & overtime pay for starters. More important, they’ve demonstrated the power we have when we work together to pressure those in control. Let’s keep that spirit alive and make it work for us all! Bring a non perishable food item to help out a neighbor, and enjoy how uplifting it feels to stand shoulder to shoulder with like minded friends and neighbors.
We are a peaceful, inclusive coalition standing for justice, dignity, and equality for all. United across identities and experiences, we fight against racial injustice, economic inequality, xenophobia, homophobia, transphobia, ableism, sexism, and the systemic neglect of veterans and marginalized communities.
Our mission is to create a world where every person—regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, ability, immigration status, or background—is treated with respect, compassion, and fairness. We reject hate in all its forms and stand firmly against racism, fascism, misogyny, and authoritarianism.
Through nonviolent protest, community education, and unwavering solidarity, we work to empower people, defend democracy, and build a future rooted in kindness, courage, and shared humanity.
We believe in the inherent value of every life. We believe in love over fear. And we believe that change begins with all of us—together.
WE RISE UP in collaboration with Torch Of Texas will be collecting non-parishable food items to benefit the local food pantry ABUNDANT HARVEST.

title: Hands Along High Street

address_lines: Eight miles along High St. from Rt. 161 in Worthington south to downtown Columbus

description:
# We Stand United!

**THIS IS A MULTISTEP SIGN UP PROCESS!** Please read all the way to the end of this message. 

**NOTE** that the address given for this event (3923 N High St.) is a **PLACEHOLDER.** The event takes place along the entire 8-mile stretch of High Street between Rt. 161 in Worthington and downtown Columbus. 

Before you finish signing up here, please go to the [Hands Along High Street SignUp Genius page](https://www.signupgenius.com/go/9040F44AAAF2FA3F58-57596461-hands#/) to pick the exact location where you will be stationed during the protest (the Sign Up slot you pick has the actual address where you will meet). Then come back here and complete your registration.

**Read more about this unique event here:**

Join the final big resistance event of the summer before the beginning of the new school year! With your participation, we will form a **human chain of resistance** 8 miles long on the public sidewalk along the west side of High Street from Route 161 in Worthington to downtown Columbus, delivering the message that **WE STAND UNITED** in defense of fundamental American values and against the corruption and tyranny of the Trump administration.
 
This will be unlike any previous rally in Ohio, and signup is a bit different too. You can confirm your participation here, but to ensure that we have an unbroken chain, we also need to know where along the route you plan to be. So once you’ve finished here, please go to the [Hands Along High Street SignUp Genius page](https://www.signupgenius.com/go/9040F44AAAF2FA3F58-57596461-hands#/) and choose a location along the route. This will help our planning to make this event a success. 

**NOTE:** We will have a Moment of Unity where we link hands to form an 8-mile human chain. But leading up to that moment, we want the people of Columbus to know why we’re here. Please bring your protest signs, American flags, cowbells, etc. 

This is a family-friendly, peaceful event. Once you complete your registration, you will receive details about a day that we hope to remember for years to come!

title: March for Integrity (Madison)
description:
This is a bannering event on the pedestrian bridge that starts at 1800 Farm pl, Madison, WI and stretches across Campus dr.

The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: Brookline Rally for Democracy 09/06/2025
description:
Brookline Rally for Democracy


Join us every Saturday, 2:00-3:00 pm for a peaceful, pro-democracy rally at Coolidge Corner in Brookline as we raise our voices against the abuses of the Trump administration.

We stand for:

o  Immigrant rights, human rights, and anti-racism

o  Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

o  Healthcare and Social Security

o  The protection of our planet

We stand for empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and an end to the devastating wars in Gaza, Ukraine, and Iran. We stand for democracy, justice, and a future we can be proud to leave to the next generation.

This will be a spirited, peaceful gathering—bring your voice, your friends, and your signs! All are welcome, including participants with walkers, wheelchairs, scooters, and other mobility devices.

This weekly event is hosted by Speak Out, Seniors! and we invite all generations to join us in standing up for democracy—one rally at a time. We'll continue this weekly tradition for as long as it takes!

Suggestions:

o  Bring a water bottle, sunscreen, and a hat

o  In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same!
accessibility_notes: All are welcome, including participants with walkers, wheelchairs, scooters, and other mobility devices.

title: Human Rights Rally

sponsor.name: Shifting The Dream:  A Carceral Human Rights Task Force in partnership with Prisoners' Rights Kansas

location.venue: South Severance Street along the East Side Cemetery Across from HCF
address_lines: S Severance St between Avenue C and Avenue F

description:
Rally for Human Rights of Prisoners.
We can change this.  We will change this. 
What is this? 
These men are living in filth, many don't have toilet paper or hand soap and have to eat with feces on their hands.  They swelter in 100 degree heat, wear the same dirty clothes for days on end, endure a constant cycle of lockdowns, and live with standing water.  They must choose between the endless line for food or the endless line for medicine.  They are not allowed to even buy paper to write a letter home, or even write to an attorney.    They are left to languish in a concrete maze, silenced, straitjacketed by a lack of information about their basic rights, alone, and voiceless.  
Do not despair! Stand with us as free people for these men and women and be their voice, be their defender.  We are not powerless!  We are not helpless! We are not voiceless! We will speak for them! We will stand for them! We CAN! We absolutely CAN! And we WILL!
accessibility_notes: This is a rally held in public space on the side of the road.  There is no sidewalk.  We will assist you in any way we can.

description:

The Baltimore-based empire of right-wing TV mogul David Smith [destroys the local Baltimore economy](https://therealnews.com/ethics-expert-sinclair-broadcasting-disclose-business-conflicts-baltimore), [discriminates against people of color](https://baltimorefishbowl.com/stories/whats-behind-the-dont-eat-atlas-beef/), and through its network of hundreds of local Fox affiliates broadcasts [lies and misinformation](https://fair.org/home/how-sinclair-sneaks-right-wing-spin-into-millions-of-households/) that undermine our democracy!

description:
**Featuring**

+ Former Congressman Beto O’Rourke

+ Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35)

+ Rep. Gina Hinojosa (HD-49)

+ Rep. Lauren Ashley Simmons (HD-146)

+ Mia Balderas, MOVE Texas Action Fund

+ Leonard Aguilar, Texas AFL-CIO Secretary-Treasurer 


***Wear a white shirt to join in resistance!***

Governor Greg Abbott is letting Trump take over Texas. Instead of addressing the real crises Texans are facing, he is using the special legislative session to push Trump’s political agenda. While families recover from the devastating Central Texas floods, lawmakers are wasting time redrawing voting maps behind closed doors to cling to power.

The first step in the Trump Take Over are field hearings to get public comment on their power grab. We need to show up and speak out. Canal Street is one of the most dangerous streets in Manhattan, and is a DOT designated senior priority corridor under Vision Zero. We cannot stand by while the City continues to let pedestrians and cyclists die or get seriously injured. The community has fought for a redesign for years. The time is now to Fix Canal Street.

Join us for a rally telling Mayor Adams we need safety NOW, and for a vigil honoring those whose lives were taken on Canal Street this past weekend.

LUCE Principles: 
We are a coalition of immigrant-led, grassroots organizations who build people power for everyone across Massachusetts.  We move grounded in our principles of justice and equity, with a deep commitment to keeping all of our communities safe through grassroots organizing, information sharing, and mutual aid. 

LUCE Vision:
We hold a collective vision for a People’s immigration justice, and refuse to accept that meeting one demand means not meeting another. While we may focus on a particular demand that uplifts a particular community, we refuse to leave anyone behind because of their marginalized identity.

We know that all of us are deserving of collective liberation. We organize in solidarity with Black, Indigenous, and People of Color, immigrants and refugees, people who are targets of criminalization and currently or formerly incarcerated, young people, elders, LGBTQ+ people, and all those who are oppressed and living at the margins due to the broken system of “justice” within the U.S.

title: Defend Due Process
description:
DEFEND DUE PROCESS
(Rage Against the Regime)
August 2, 2025
10:00 AM - 12PM
Falls Park, 601 S Main St, Greenville, SC

Join us on Saturday, August 2 at Falls Park to DEFEND DUE PROCESS, because the Constitution doesn’t come with exceptions.

Across the country, and right here in Greenville County, we are witnessing alarming attacks on the foundational rights that protect all people, not just citizens. Our local sheriff has secretly expanded the county’s involvement in the ICE 287(g) program through a new Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), without public input or council approval. This policy gives deputies federal immigration powers, bypasses due process, and threatens families who have lived, worked, and contributed to this community for years.

But the attacks on justice don’t stop there.
South Carolina officials are now entertaining a proposal to build an “Alligator Alcatraz”, a bizarre, wasteful project that symbolizes everything wrong with our state’s priorities, surveillance over service, incarceration over compassion.

This protest is about more than policies, it’s about principles.
It’s about defending the Constitution, the right to due process, and the very idea that justice belongs to everyone.

WHAT WE’RE FIGHTING FOR
	•	Constitutional due process for every person
	•	Transparency and accountability in local government
	•	An end to racial profiling and ICE collaboration in our county
	•	Rejection of wasteful, authoritarian projects like “Alligator Alcatraz”

This movement is powered by regular people, immigrants, veterans, parents, neighbors, who believe in liberty and justice for all.

Bring your signs, your friends, and your voice.
Because when our rights are on the line, silence is not an option.

Join us to rally in support of democracy and against the coup engineered by Musk and Trump! Bring a sign and a friend!

Chants and songs are welcome. However, please remember:

We practice peaceful non-violence and non-confrontation. Although we are all very concerned about Elon Musk' s activities and unconstitutional meddling in our democracy, we protest peacefully and with comradery among those who support refusing to go along with Trump and Musk.

**So, if you encounter cybertrucks or hecklers, DO NOT RESPOND! We do not heckle those who have opposing views.**

Peaceful non-violence means that if any violence or confrontation occurs, we sit down and go silent. 

Marshals are present to protect us all and will assist. Columbus Dialogue Police will help de-escalate any confrontation. This has been an amazing group of demonstrators. Let's build friendships!

Let your reps and senators know how we feel! Meet others who share your views, and help build community.

description:

The Constitution grants Congress the power of the purse, but Trump is ignoring Congress' budgets, levying new taxes, and converting taxpayer dollars into useless crypto.

The Constitution gives Congress the sole authority to declare war, but Trump is threatening our friendly neighbors with economic ruin and military action, citing blatantly deceitful justifications.

description:

We invite others who feel the same way to join the Movement.  You do not need to be old, you do not need to be in Baltimore, and you do not need to stand on Wednesdays, but we ask that you use the Wednesday Movement banner.

It’s easy:
​Reach out to friends and neighbors
​Make some signs (one should say “We Are The Wednesday Movement)
​Pick a day, time, and location that works for your group
​And spread the word
This is a grassroots initiative. It has the potential to change the world.  Join with us and help make it happen!

Contact Anne George, 443-831-7528 for more information on initiating a sign wave in your area.

title: I91 Overpass Visibility Standout - Longmeadow

location.venue: Bark Haul Road (at the I91 overpass)

description:

If You Bring a Sign, Banner, or Flag For sign and banner lettering, bigger is better, so it can be easily read from the roadway. Flags are great, too. Wouldn't it be amazing to reclaim our flag? Mass DOT does not like things attached to the fence. They may visit, so be prepared to not have anything attached. Never drape anything over the fence, even with ropes, because it would be very dangerous if it accidentally fell onto the highway. Other Logistics No Port-A-Potties are available. Please take everything you brought away with you and leave the site totally clean. About These Standouts

Come join like-minded folks to demand that Trump, Musk, and the Republican-led Congress stop their unconstitutional power grab and the cruel destruction of our federal government.

We will hold banners, signs, and flags, and we'll wave to passing motorists. Many will beep and wave back at us, which feels nice! We'll show people that they're not alone and help give them the courage to join us and take a stand.

Please come out whether or not you have a sign or banner or flag. More people is better!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 hour and 15 minute standout.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational and non-violent, in words and body language. 

We welcome your energy and ideas, and we're looking forward to meeting everyone. Let's have some fun and make some good trouble

title: March for Integrity (National)
description:
The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and **across the country**, where we expect to mobilize **millions of Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: Four Corners in Lenexa  Standing Rally
description: As citizens, we can’t let the policies and actions of the Federal Government and unelected billionaires be normalized, but we can only stop what’s going on by coming together.  A STANDING RALLY  will draw attention to the situation, encouraging our neighbors to join with us. We will rally every Saturday morning from 11 AM – 12 PM.  Stay for the full hour or come by when and for how long you can. We will peacefully line the sidewalk on all four corners of 87th Parkway and Maurer Road,  holding signs on issues that are most meaningful to us or just simply standing in support of our neighbors and our country.  If sitting is more comfortable for you, you are very welcome to bring mobility or lawn chairs!! There is room for everyone!
accessibility_notes:
Here are a couple of notes on logistics.
Please be especially mindful of parking.  For example, if you live relatively nearby, please consider walking.  If you drive, there is street parking on the residential streets to the north and also a bit further on the south.  About ½ mile down on the west, there is a large civic campus garage at 17201 W 87th St. Pkwy.  In addition, on the SE, SW, and NW sides of the intersection, there are restaurants and shops with big, but commercially owned parking lots meant for customers. Note that Lenexa Point on the NW side has recently put up signs, saying they will tow non-customer cars. (Also note that if you become a customer, it’s fine to bring snacks to the rally that you have bought, but please take any empty snack containers back home with you, when you leave. In any case, no matter which direction you are coming from, if it is possible, please try to park before you reach the intersection to save on congestion and choose a spot as far away as you feel comfortable walking from, leaving closer spots to those who can’t walk as far.
The rally will start on the SE corner, but as more folks arrive, we will disperse to the SW, NW, and NE corners, as well.   If you cross from one side to another, please pay particular attention to cars turning right as you cross! 
 Participants should bring their own signs (if they want to hold them).  Note that sticks supporting the signs can’t be pointed at either end.  Also, in designing content for the signs, please remember that children will be present.  
Please stand only along the sidewalks parallel to the street and not on the grass.  However, also be sure to allow pedestrian access to the sidewalk and businesses.   We are not expecting issues, but keep in mind that a core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action.  Remember to de-escalate any potential confrontation with someone,  who disagrees with you. And of course, follow directions from our excellent Lenexa police, if asked.
We will not have speakers. The plan will simply be to hold the signs we have made and wave, if that feels right.  We expect that a lot of passing cars will honk back in approval! 
Finally, please note that all our organizers will be wearing lanyards with badges reading  “Standing Rally Corner Captain or “Standing Rally Media/City Liaison”.  If you see other folks with “Press” marked on their clothing or who are giving direction to you, know that they are not part of Four Corners and are not endorsed or vetted by us.
See you soon.  Let’s show our neighbors “what Democracy Looks Like”!!
P.S.  If you want to post an inspiring (!) story about your experience, please add #FourCornersinLenexa to your post!

description:
Join us EVERY Saturday at 12pm to protest Elon Musk and his unconstitutional dismantling of the federal government. Bring a sign, your friends, musical instruments, whatever makes you happy.

Elon Musk may have faded into the shadows but DOGE is still engaged in an administrative coup of the federal government. Musk and his crew have also stolen untold amounts of private data from various federal agencies, possibly the largest data breach in history.

They've caused immense harm by dismantling USAID and have set their sights on everything from Social Security to the NIH and FAA next. Make no mistake, their end goal is the destruction of the US Federal Government and its ability to check corporate power and provide basic services.

How this develops in Washington remains to be seen, but as US citizens we can exercise our 1st Amendment right to peacefully protest. Elon Musk's access to money is largely based on Tesla stock, which is currently valued at 15-20 times that of other car companies. Driving down the share price is a direct attack on Elon's power.

The stakes couldn’t be higher. No one is coming to save us—not politicians, not the media. It's up to the people to stand up and fight for democracy and against fascism.

Let me reiterate, this is meant to be a peaceful protest and we cannot legally obstruct Tesla business or block the driveways. I would also ask that you not harass Tesla owners that come into the dealership as that's counter productive and antagonizes people who probably bought their cars before these events took place.

title: "Moral Monday" Street Rally

address_lines: N. Main St. and W. Division St.

description:
Please join us in opposing cuts to essential safety net programs!

Please join us at recurring  "Moral Monday" street rallies in River Falls WI.

Our “Moral Monday” street rally in River Falls is on Mondays, from 4PM to 6PM, at the intersection of Main and Division Streets, where we will hold signs and stand along the public sidewalks.

Folks may join for part or all the two hours, and may bring their own signs or use signs we’ll have to share.

If the weather is bad—hard rain, high wind, and/or lightening—we’ll cancel that week’s rally.

Our "Moral Monday" street rallies are inspired and informed by work of the prominent North Carolina pastor and anti-poverty activist the Rev. William Barber, who founded the Center for Public Theology and Public Policy at Yale and now teaches there.

On the twelfth anniversary of his first "Moral Monday" demonstration, Monday April 28, 2025, Rev. Barber was arrested for praying against the Republican-led budget while in the Rotunda of our US Capitol. At a rally held before he entered the Rotunda to pray, Rev. Barber said: “Forty-three percent of women and almost half of all children are poor and low income. Somebody ought to say something … Somebody gotta challenge this budget.”

We are holding "Moral Monday" street rallies to voice our challenges.

We oppose Republican-approved Congressional budget resolutions that harm the poorest and most vulnerable of Americans in order to give more than $5-trillion in tax breaks to the richest and most privileged of Americans.

We oppose budget proposals that eliminate or make draconian cuts to federal programs for child care, health research, education, housing assistance, community development, and the elderly.

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are not just public policy choices, they are moral choices. 

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are morally wrong, not just bad public policy choices. 

Please join with us to "say something" and "challenge this budget".

title: Protest Elon Musk's Illegal Government Takeover #TeslaTakedown - Stanford Saturdays
description:
PLEASE READ COMPLETELY before attending!

This is a peaceful, nonviolent protest on the sidewalk in front of the Stanford Tesla showroom. There will be theatrics and dancing. Get ready to improv! We'll also be looping through Stanford Shopping Mall with peaceful positive energy. Of course you may opt out and continue to demonstrate in front of the Tesla showroom. 

We know making lots of noise is typically part of a good protest. But most protests aren’t right across the street from a Ronald McDonald House. Let’s take care to keep our noise levels down to a dull roar. Bring your energy and spirit, but let’s refrain from the cowbells, drums and car honks. We can get our point across without interfering with our neighbors on the other side of the road.

Wear your favorite wig, big hat, or costume. We want to have fun and to feel like a party during our demonstrations! Signs, flags, and similar items are welcome.

This is a peaceful demonstration, and any conflicts or altercations will not be tolerated. Walk away if one arises and report it to the demonstration leader on site if it is a serious altercation. We will comply with requests from the police and mall security, including if we are asked to leave. By the way, we have already have a fantastic relationship with mall security, which is a plus!

Do not boo or confront Tesla drivers or cars, or Tesla employees. Remember that most Tesla drivers are our allies, and many are protesting with us!

Please Note: Photos may be taken and published at this event, including by attendees and professional photographers. If you prefer not to have your image captured or shared, please take your own precautions (e.g., wear a mask, hat, or wig).

#BoycottTesla #DivestFromTesla

title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ ICE/U.S. Immigration Court in Phoenix
description:

**When we realized the ICE was abducting people appearing at U.S. Immigration Court, we decided it would be the perfect place for an ICE-specific RhRR!**

Every Tuesday @ 7:00 am, we'll gather on the southwest corner where 7th Ave, Van Buren, and Grand meet, right in front of the Social Security Administration office, which also serves as U.S. Immigration Court.

**STAY ON THE SIDEWALK**! It's public property and we've a right to be there. Be sure you **DO NOT BLOCK** access to the building—that means cars as well as people.

**Please make ICE-specific signs**, as we're here to show the busy morning commuters that they are not alone, the ICE agents that We The People care about due process for everyone, and those before the court that we support them. Because no human is illegal.

Spread the word. Come join us. All the details you need are at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).
